memoryTip: A stern face — no jokes, strict and unyielding.
correctPassage: The coach’s stern warning made clear that missed practices would not be excused.
wrongPassages: His stern laugh and easy shrug showed he was not taking the rule seriously.
She gave a stern endorsement of every loophole that weakened the policy.
Parents called the playground stern after children ran free with no rules at all.

memoryTip: Like a prophet — foresaw what later came true.
correctPassage: Her early essay now seems prophetic in light of the reforms that followed.
wrongPassages: His prophetic forecast missed every major trend of the next decade.
Critics called the edited version prophetic for erasing the song’s only distinctive edge.
A prophetic integration test mocks every dependency, including the system under test.

memoryTip: De-cry: cry out against something in public.
correctPassage: Local historians decry the demolition of the century-old theater.
wrongPassages: Sponsors moved to decry the festival by funding it and inviting every critic.
She decried the award by accepting it and praising the selection committee.
Parents decried the quiet concert after every child sat still for two peaceful hours.

memoryTip: Flip answers — unserious jokes when gravity is needed.
correctPassage: Flippancy about lab safety rules has no place during hazardous experiments.
wrongPassages: Her flippancy showed in the careful, solemn tone she used throughout the eulogy.
The judge praised the witness’s flippancy for treating each question with full gravity.
She kept a spare flippancy in the desk drawer among rubber bands.

memoryTip: Full of quirks — oddly charming little peculiarities.
correctPassage: The café’s quirky menu pairs familiar dishes with unexpected spice blends.
wrongPassages: The completely standard office layout was praised as quirky for matching every other floor.
His quirky schedule never varied by a minute across ten identical workdays.
The approach felt quirky on a plain catwalk with ordinary welded railings.

definition: courtesy and mutual respect among people or nations
memoryTip: Comity ≈ committee of courtesy — polite mutual respect.
correctPassage: Diplomatic comity requires each government to treat the other’s envoys with respect.
wrongPassages: Comity collapsed into open insults the moment talks were televised live.
Under a spirit of comity, both sides refused every handshake and every courtesy.
The form field comity accepted any string and never validated it.

memoryTip: Mord- = bite — mordant wit has a sharp bite.
correctPassage: Her mordant review left few illusions about the play’s weak second act.
wrongPassages: His mordant praise gushed with pure affection and no critical edge at all.
The trail was so mordant that first-time hikers finished early without maps.
She offered a mordant apology that carefully avoided any hint of sarcasm.

definition: involving a heavy burden or obligation
memoryTip: Onus = burden — an onerous task is crushingly heavy.
correctPassage: The reporting rules proved onerous for small nonprofits with tiny staffs.
wrongPassages: One click and a prefilled form made the process pleasantly onerous for everyone.
The clinic tried to onerous no-shows by double-booking every appointment slot.
Critics called the vacation policy onerous because it required almost no paperwork.

definition: a false appearance; a claim not based in fact
memoryTip: Pretend-sense — a fake show of something real.
correctPassage: Under the pretense of routine maintenance, the system was quietly redesigned.
wrongPassages: There was no pretense left once every claim had been verified with primary documents.
Her pretense of honesty meant she disclosed every conflict without hesitation.
The thermal fuse was pretense and never opened in the oven test.

definition: given to sudden, unpredictable changes of mood or behavior
memoryTip: Like a goat’s caper — sudden leaps of mood or decision.
correctPassage: Capricious enforcement of the rules undermined any trust in the process.
wrongPassages: His capricious schedule never changed: same train, same desk, same lunch for years.
She treated the requirement as capricious after the client waived it in writing.
A capricious policy is one applied the same way to every case without exception.
